title: Test Heuristics Deck — SFDIPOT and HICCUPPS(F) at the Card Table
description: A deck of sixteen cards for two well-known testing heuristics: the SFDIPOT product elements from James Bach's Heuristic Test Strategy Model and the HICCUPPS(F) consistency oracles from James Bach and Michael Bolton, each paraphrased and applied to a fictional bill-splitting feature. Jot test ideas on any card (or start from its prompts), deal yourself an empty card, and watch a two-ring coverage wheel fill in before exporting the ideas as a Markdown checklist.
prompt: Build 'Test Heuristics Deck', an interactive guide to two testing heuristics, attributed correctly: SFDIPOT (Structure, Function, Data, Interfaces, Platform, Operations, Time) from James Bach's Heuristic Test Strategy Model, and the HICCUPPS consistency oracles (History, Image, Comparable products, Claims, User expectations, Product, Purpose, Statutes) from James Bach and Michael Bolton, with the common F for Familiar problems. Apply them to a fictional feature: every card prompts test ideas for it, I can jot my own ideas on each card, and a coverage wheel fills in as I go. Write every description in your own words, and make it feel like a card table rather than a slide deck.

methodology: Content oracle: both mnemonics are checked letter by letter and name by name against the published lists, and the header is checked for the attribution to James Bach and to Bach and Bolton.
State-to-visual mapping: each wheel segment exposes data-level (0–3, capped), so filling a card is asserted on the segment, the pip count, the total and the coverage percentage together.
Navigation equivalence: the same card can be reached from the wheel (click and Enter), the mini-card fan (click and Arrow keys, with wrap-around) and the Previous/Next buttons.
Seeded randomness with an invariant: 'Deal me an empty card' is called fifteen times and must never land on a card that already has ideas, then must find the single remaining empty card.
Persistence and export: reload keeps the ideas, and the Markdown export has one checklist line per idea and marks exactly the empty cards.
risks: Misattribution or a wrong letter in either mnemonic, which would undermine the page's credibility.
Two cards with the same letter (I, C, P, S, F) colliding if anything keyed on the letter instead of a stable id.
SVG arc paths going wrong for small segments, or the focus ring on a segment being invisible.
The sticky wheel covering the card on small screens (it becomes static below 900 px).
qa.playwright: Content checks read the deck through window.__heur and the fan buttons, so they compare the actual mnemonic order rather than CSS layout. SVG wheel segments are focusable g elements with role=button, and Playwright clicks and focuses them like any other element through data-testid plus data-id. The random deal runs under ?seed=5, but the test asserts an invariant (never a card with ideas) instead of a fixed sequence, which keeps it robust if the deck changes. Screenshots aren't asserted because the serif fallback differs by OS.
coverage: Prompt-to-idea, idea levels on the wheel, blank-input rejection, removing an idea
Navigation by wheel click, Enter on a segment, Previous/Next and Arrow keys with wrap
Deal-an-empty-card invariant, persistence across reload, Markdown export

a11y: Every card in both fans is a button with its full name and idea count, and Arrow keys move through the deck; wheel segments are focusable buttons with the same labels, so the wheel is never the only way in. The current card and the coverage summary are polite live regions, and the idea input has a proper label.
